# Burnly v0.1.31

Introduces graceful cloud session expiration handling, secure OS keyring credential eviction on terminal auth errors, background sync quiescence, and an inline desktop re-authentication recovery flow.

## Highlights

- **Terminal auth session invalidation.** When cloud token refresh encounters terminal authentication failures (`AUTH_REFRESH_TOKEN_EXPIRED`, `AUTH_REFRESH_TOKEN_INVALID`, `AUTH_REFRESH_TOKEN_REUSED`, `AUTH_SESSION_REVOKED`), Burnly immediately purges expired credentials from memory and the OS keyring.
- **Inline session recovery UI.** Settings now displays `<email> · Session expired` with an actionable `[Sign in again]` button, allowing users to re-authenticate directly via PKCE without requiring an initial manual sign-out step.
- **Sync quiescence & error suppression.** Background usage synchronization stops cleanly when a session expires, suppressing raw technical error codes (`AUTH_REFRESH_TOKEN_EXPIRED`) from cluttering the settings view.
- **Actionable re-authentication error feedback.** If re-authentication fails (such as for suspended accounts or network reachability issues), the specific user-facing failure explanation is surfaced directly in the settings view.
- **Concurrency & storage consistency.** Refresh error handling guards against races between in-flight network calls and concurrent user sign-out or new logins, ensuring only unchanged active sessions are cleared and memory never diverges from persistent storage.

## Privacy

Burnly continues to read usage-only metadata. It selects model identity, token
counters, and generation timestamps; it never reads prompt text, response
content, tool invocations, project paths, or sensitive credentials.

## Install

### Linux

Run:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://github.com/fikrilal/burnly/releases/latest/download/install-linux.sh | sh
```

For a pinned install of this release:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://github.com/fikrilal/burnly/releases/download/v0.1.31/install-linux.sh | BURNLY_VERSION=v0.1.31 sh
```

### Windows Preview

Download the Windows x64 installer from this release:

```text
burnly-v0.1.31-windows-x86_64.exe
```

The Windows preview installer is not Authenticode-signed. Windows may show an
unknown publisher or SmartScreen warning. Only download Burnly from the
official GitHub release and verify the published `SHA256SUMS`. Tauri updater
artifacts remain cryptographically signed.

### macOS Preview

Run:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://github.com/fikrilal/burnly/releases/latest/download/install-macos.sh | sh
```

For a pinned install of this release:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://github.com/fikrilal/burnly/releases/download/v0.1.31/install-macos.sh | BURNLY_VERSION=v0.1.31 sh
```

Manual `.dmg` installation is also available:

```text
burnly-v0.1.31-macos-aarch64.dmg
burnly-v0.1.31-macos-x86_64.dmg
```

The macOS preview is unsigned and not notarized. If Gatekeeper blocks the
downloaded app, clear quarantine once after copying it to Applications:

```bash
xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/Burnly.app
```

## Verification

This release was verified with local unit and integration tests across `CloudSession`,
`AccountService`, Tauri IPC contracts, and React UI components, including concurrency
barrier tests for race conditions between in-flight refresh and concurrent sign-in/out.

Release artifacts include `SHA256SUMS`, GitHub build provenance, signed updater
artifacts, `latest.json`, and the `latest-linux.json` compatibility alias.
